critique: At t4 the render convincingly shows a rich field of small amber-gold luminous dust over a near-black background, with soft additive-looking halos. However, t1 remains far too sparse, reading as isolated motes rather than a continuous suspended dust field; the large density jump by t4 reads as particle accumulation rather than a stable atmospheric field with clearly trackable upward drift. A few oversized bright motes also stand out against the otherwise fine scale.

suggestions.why: Raise the birth rate so the t1 frame immediately contains enough fine dust rather than requiring several seconds to build density.
Shorten lifetime to prevent the higher birth rate from making t4 excessively dense, producing a more consistent dust-field density across both sampled times.
Reduce size variation so fewer particles become conspicuously large bright blobs and the field retains a finer dust scale.
